openings.name: wing root, right
openings.why: the rocker's spar socket carries the wing spar out through the pod's side at the wing root and sweeps the full stroke; the wing's own drag model starts there

openings.name: wing root, left
openings.why: the left rocker's spar socket, as the right: out through the pod's side at the wing root, through the full stroke

openings.name: horn slots
openings.why: each rocker's horn (its arm, boss and pin) and the coupler eye on it ride inside the shoulder span, beside the wing root, and rise above the loft at the top of the stroke: a slot in the pod's top over the shoulders; their exposed sweep counts in the drag

openings.name: boom posts
openings.why: the tail boom runs above the pod (over the shoulders it must clear the horn eyes' sweep), so each gearbox plate's post rises through a slot in the pod's top to its boom clamp; the exposed post and pad count in the drag

openings.name: pitot
openings.why: the probe reads the free stream ahead of the nose, so it leaves the nose through a hole of its own diameter; its exposed tip counts in the drag

outside.why: it runs above the pod from the forward clamp to the tail (it never enters the loft)
on the exposed boom, screwed to the aft plate's post
on the exposed boom, screwed to the forward plate's post

plate journals: a flanged bushing's flange on the plate's outer face, its body through the plate inward; a bearing flush with the outer face, inward

frame (structure.airframe): rails from the aft housing's sleeve to the forward plate's outer face; panels between the plate planes; boom clamps on the plates' outer faces with the screw flange below the boom; trays as channels, flanges up, from the plate face for their stated length

current_sense.basis: 40 A/V over 3.3 V at 12 bits (STM32F405 ADC, 12-bit; the ST page was not readable this round)
current_sense.hardware: F405-WMO with a PDB whose shunt is NOT marked "3m0" (Matek notice Dec.22, 2025: a 3m0 PDB reads 13.2 A full scale and suits only < 15 A aircraft; its owner gets a new PDB from the dealer). The 40 A/V scale is the specification's 132 A sense.
not_read_by: the crank governor and drive clamp (crank encoder and the FC voltage sense only)

assumptions: Section polar e387-film: cd factor 1.2 for film over ribs: an assumption with no published source
Motor rotor inertia estimated from mass and diameter; not published.
Battery internal resistance estimated from claimed C rate; not published.
ESC efficiency 0.95 assumed.
Servo current is the SPEC M8 estimate: stall current x (torque / stall torque), idle if published.
Tail polar is an assumed thin plate.
Gear trains mix steel pinions or gears with acetal mates of the same module; each gear is held to its own published rating.

Twist servo at the elbow drives the hand wing through a mtube-tigertitanium-ti3al2.5v-6.35x5.54 tube; M7 checks its torsion against the published minimum yield through von Mises (tau = sigma_y / sqrt 3).
Twist horn linkage ratio is geometry: the servo's published torque and speed are scaled by it; linkage backlash and compliance not modelled.

Round 5: the crank-speed governor and the 26 A drive-current clamp run in our controller on the flight controller at 960 Hz, reading the crank angle from the sensor-rls-orbis-br10 (14-bit; speed from 2-sample differences) and the battery voltage from the FC's sense input (0.01692 V resolution); the duty computed at one tick is applied at the next (one period of latency, held in between). The ESC is assumed to apply the commanded duty linearly; the clamp is a duty limit from measured speed and voltage with the motor's published Kv and resistance (its resistance at temperature is not modelled).
Round 5: the twist schedule takes the crank phase from the same encoder (last sample advanced at the measured speed); the servo PWM refresh is not modelled.
One crank pin drives both couplers; the left wing flies its own mirrored linkage (left-right stroke difference in design.packing).
Round 5: fixed stroke, half-swing 38.0 deg: the coupler pins are pinned in the rockers (no slot, no stroke servo); thrust and lift are set by stroke frequency and twist.

Rigid elbow: the outer spar is bonded into the inner one (spigot); round 5 removes the arm wing's own twist (twist weight 0 at the elbow), so the arm wing flies at its fixed incidence and only the hand wing twists.
Derived parts: pitot-static probe (bases in the structure list); pitot pressure lines counted in the 15% margin with the wiring.

Round 5: every drive joint has its own rated bearing, bushing or rod end (structure.joints states which force each reacts); loads combine at every step in the flight model, as magnitudes (directions not credited). Round 6: the first pinion on an outboard bearing (structure.joints, motor shaft outboard); shafts, pins, seats, rockers, coupler links and keys in structure.members.

Stroke envelope measured by flight test in calm air at a fraction of the gear, spar, coupler, servo and bearing ratings (control.envelopeAllowance: a rough-air allowance, a design choice); M7 judges full ratings on the flown loads.

Round 6: the 20 ms control delay applies to the crank governor and drive clamp as to attitude control: the duty the ESC applies was computed ceil(0.02 x rate) controller periods earlier (20.8 ms at 960 Hz), and the twist schedule takes its crank phase from that same tick (the encoder sample then, advanced at the speed measured then). The stroke-frequency command reaching the governor has already passed the attitude controller's 20 ms delay, so that path sees 40 ms (conservative).

Round 6: every loaded part of the drive is sized from a catalogue metal with published strength (structure.members, src/design/linkage.js): forces summed as magnitudes (directions not credited); shaft moments bounded at supports and load planes; pins judged at their roots, bosses by the rigid-pin edge pressure; shoulder pins clamped by the rocker hub between their bushings; seats without a published bearing strength judged at the tensile yield; aluminium typical strengths (AA, NOT FOR DESIGN) at half value; stress concentrations at keyseats and shoulders not modelled (static, ductile).

Round 6: an outboard bearing on the motor shaft in the forward plate carries the first pinion with the motor bearing nearest it as the second support no closer than 5.0 mm (motor bearing positions not published): rated at F (a + s) / s.
Round 6: the F405-WMO is specified with a PDB whose shunt is not marked 3m0 (Matek notice, Dec.22, 2025); the battery current limit reads current through it at the specification's 40 A/V.

Round 7: the flight controller runs at 240 Hz and ticks at fixed instants; the M4 air is convected at the rough-air speed (Dryden filters, rotary terms and gust durations), so every input is the same function of time at both steps of the half-step check (out/verification/evidence/M7-inputs-<design>.json).
Round 7: leading-edge suction eta_s per strip from the measured table (3 points, data/calibration/suction.json) at the design's own cruise effective-angle amplitudes; the 0.6 default is not used.

Round 8: every part reaches the airframe through a rated path (structure.airframe, src/design/airframe.js): ISO 898-1 M3 class 10.9 screws at their minimum proof load (shear by von Mises on it), Araldite 2011 at half its typical lap shear on the substrate, HellermannTyton ties at their minimum loop strength; the frame parts are positioned in the design file but not packed by the film checker, and their clearances are reported.

Round 8: inertial loads on carried parts are bounded by m (|f_origin| + r |wdot| + r |w|^2) from the flight model at every step (load channels sf_origin, wdot, w2); the tail by its aerodynamic force tail_F.
Round 8: TECS pitch weights height-first above the floor band (spdWeight 0.5); hand-launch climb command 3 m/s.

Round 9: pin-in-hole bearing below the source's edge distance is the lesser of that source at half and EN 1999-1-1 / EN 1993-1-8 bolt bearing (k1 alpha_b fu / 1.25, specified-minimum fu) at the seat's own distances, every seat at e >= 1.2 d0; rings are judged with e = D / 2 in every direction. EN 1999-1-1 does not list EN AW-7075: its expression is applied with 7075-T6's specified minimum fu.

Round 9: gear ratings are KHK's catalogue values corrected to the design's conditions (structure.gear_stages[].rating_check): mating gear by JGMA 402-01 d01 i/(i+1) and KH-beta (the "weak shaft" column wherever a gear is not at mid-span: KHK states no criterion for "rugged"), JGMA 401-01 Y-epsilon; speed by JGMA's KV on the gear's accuracy row at both speeds (round 10) and ZV (below 1 m/s the curve's first value, as KHK's own 600 rpm ratings need); the oil at or above 100 cSt (50 C) and over 1e7 cycles with no credit; Duracon by KHK's plastic method (KV, KM 0.75 Duracon on Duracon) and JGMA 401's 2/3 for the reversing load. KHK states the JGMA method for module 1.5 and up; these gears are module 1, as KHK's own ratings are. Rating crank frequency 4 Hz.
Round 9: hand release at 8 m/s, the design's named speed (SPEC ruling after round 8).

Round 10: gear accuracy rows for JGMA KV: N5 as old JIS grade 1, N7 as 3, N8 as 4 (KHK Japanese reference Table 8.4), unmodified teeth (no modification stated); the KV ratio is applied at the actual speed and capped at 1 (no credit for running slower than rated).

Round 10: shaft-to-hub fixings without a published rating are standard RC practice (SPEC ruling): plain-bore acetal gears bonded with LOCTITE 406 on SF 770 primer, plain-bore steel with LOCTITE 638, F-Loc hubs at KHK's standard screw torque; each within the maker's published figure at full value, reported in M7 as unrated, RC practice.
Round 10: 7075-T6 seats take EN 1999-1-1's bolt-bearing expression at half (the standard does not list the alloy).

Round 10: flight step 3840 Hz: the airframe channel w2 moved 10.8% at half of 1/1920 s and 2.9% at half of 1/3840 s; the flight model's aerodynamic internal states (the lifting-line circulation, one frozen-Jacobian Newton step per flight step, and the strip lag states) advance once per step, so it converges at first order in the step.

Round 11: the section model's negative stall is kept inside the measured UIUC sweep with its own transition width (E387 stalls at -6.3 deg at Re 1e5 and 2e5, where the tables show the drag doubling; the round-10 fit had put it at -53 to -253 deg).

Round 11: a bushing is judged on the length its housing supports (structure.joints[].supports[].housing_mm): the plate thickness in an unbossed plate seat, the part's own length in a boss, shoulder housing or coupler eye.

Round 12: the belly landing is flown by the controller's own approach-and-flare law (control.landing): approach at 9.302 m/s, 1.23 x the slowest steady glide over the robustness corners (VREF per 14 CFR 25.125), feed-forward from that speed's glide row, exponential flare; field elevation known to the controller (the launch point's baro reference).

Round 12: gear life factors at the declared design life (200 flights of 1500 s, every load cycle at the M7 peak, each gear's own revolutions at the rating crank frequency): JGMA 401-01 K_L and 402-01 K_HL as KHK prints them, a count reading the table row at or above it (no source states a rule between rows); Duracon from KHK Fig. 11.3 read off the printed curve less 0.05 kgf/mm2.

Round 12: the servos run behind a Pololu step-down regulator: torque and speed at its published voltage less its 4% accuracy (or the lowest pack voltage less the dropout read off its curve), stall current at the voltage plus 4%, battery draw through the lower end of its published typical efficiency.

Round 12: the calm-air stroke envelope keeps 0.6 of every rated member's rating (rough-air member peaks measured up to 1.58 x the calm edge); the crank governor's drive clamp is 26 A; the hand launch flaps at 2.6 Hz (control.launchLaw).

Round 14: the drive planes keep 0.5 mm running clearance along the crank pin and at the plate-adjacent stages (model.js clearancePlanes); plate bushing flanges on the plate faces; rocker hubs that far clear of the shoulder bushings; Layout (SPEC layout freedom, ROUND14.set): horn stacks R fwd, L aft of their eyes between shoulder housings spread to the stacks' length; the aft plate just forward of the crank web; rails below the hinges; stage 1 overhung forward of the forward plate with the motor inside the box; the encoder (10 mm actuator) on a crank stub forward of stage 1; the stated gear fold [157.8,48.7,1.3,110.5] deg. Assembly clearance check passed (structure.clearance).

Round 15: every packed part rests on a carrier through a stated fixing (params.layout.mounts): the ESC, airspeed board, receiver and battery on the nose tray, which stands on a riser on the forward tray; the tail servos, flight controller, regulator and GPS on the aft tray; the motor on the forward plate; the crank encoder readhead on the riser by its maker's 3 x M2 and spacers; the pitot along the nose tray's flange. Support check passed; containment check passed; the fittings left outside add 705.6 mm2 at Cd 1.2 to the pod's frontal drag.

openings.name: wing root, left

openings.name: horn slots

openings.why: the probe reads the free stream ahead of the nose, so it leaves the nose through a hole of its own diameter; its exposed tip counts in the drag
